content:
Section 1 of every SOF IMO paper is pure reasoning: series, coding, directions, ranking. School maths never teaches it. Yet ten focused practice sessions routinely turn it from guesswork into banked marks. Scroll down for the free IMO Class 7 Logical Reasoning online test. Ten Olympiad-pattern MCQs, instant scoring. Under every question sits an explanation you can learn from.

What the IMO asks from Logical Reasoning in Class 7

  • Number and letter series.
  • Coding-decoding and analogies.
  • Direction sense and ranking puzzles.
  • Mirror images and embedded figures.
  • Odd-one-out and pattern completion.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • Write POSITION NUMBERS over letters (A=1 ... Z=26) — most letter series become arithmetic.
  • In direction puzzles, draw the path — never track turns in your head.
  • Ranking: total people = rank from left + rank from right − 1.
  • For mirror images, left and right swap; top and bottom do not.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Solving series by "feel" instead of writing differences.
  • Flipping top-bottom for a plain mirror question.
  • Forgetting the minus one in ranking totals.

questions.q: If ZEBRA is 26-5-2-18-1, then LION is:

questions.explanation: 26 − 15 + 1 = 12th from the left. That is L.
